description: Single source of truth for CI/local-runner gate names and status (AUDIT-27 CI-08). scripts/verify-ci-docs-drift.py enforces that docs/ci-pipeline.md, .github/workflows/*.yml, scripts/check.sh, and scripts/check-ui.mjs all agree with this file. Adding a gate here is the ONLY way to add a gate; renaming/removing one here (plus its runner/CI declarations) is the only way to remove it.

gates.label: UI unit tests
gates._note: Was ci.yml#ui-test. dev-ci.yml#ui-test runs `cd ui && npm test` (vitest) -- the same suite under the same job name.

gates.label: Go (license-server)
gates._note: Was ci.yml#go. gofmt/go vet/go test -short now run in dev-ci.yml#static-gates, verified green locally first. The pre-commit Go gate remains the only place Go is enforced on a commit.

gates.label: Panic inventory
gates._note: Was ci.yml#rust-panic-inventory, then had no CI job at all while scan-unwrap-panic.py was red. R36-12 found the redness was the SCANNER's bug -- it did not track /* */ block comments across lines, so it read the repo's audit stamps as code (6 false positives) and, in apps/cloud-server/src/redirect.rs, treated a stamp mentioning #[cfg(test)] as the start of test code and stopped checking the rest of the file (1 suppressed real finding). Fixed, triaged, and now enforced in dev-ci.yml#static-gates.

gates.label: CI docs drift
gates._note: History worth keeping: this was declared 'required' while pointing at ci.yml#ci-docs-drift, a workflow retired to .bak by 23c96330, so it enforced nothing anywhere and the status was false. It was downgraded to 'advisory' when first wired into dev-ci.yml because the checker was reporting 68 items it had no vocabulary for. R36-10 closed those out to 0 and the step is now blocking -- the stated condition. advisory_at is removed because the step no longer sets continue-on-error.

gates.label: CI path router regression test
gates._note: scripts/test-ci-routing.sh extracts the Route shell body from dev-ci.yml and runs it against 15 synthetic diffs. c5ec6381 shipped the router with no committed test, while the 0.0.36 release notes claimed one existed -- this file makes that claim true and keeps it true.

gates.label: Fuzz
gates._note: cargo-fuzz ran in ci.yml#fuzz only. The RUSTC_WRAPPER='' note recorded below is still accurate for whoever restores it.
gates.note: The fuzz job deliberately sets RUSTC_WRAPPER: '' in its job env. The ubuntu runner image globally wraps rustc with sccache, which breaks cargo-fuzz's --target build (its rustc version probe execs the resolved nightly toolchain path directly and dies with 'could not execute process sccache .../bin/rustc -vV'). The fuzz job is the only job affected (nightly + --target), so sccache must stay disabled there — do NOT re-add it. Caching is instead handled by Swatinem/rust-cache@v2 with `workspaces: fuzz` (cargo-fuzz builds into fuzz/target/, which default workspace discovery misses).

gates.label: Release workflow validation
gates._note: R36-11. release.yml was renamed to release.yml.bak by 23c96330 with an empty commit message and nothing replaced it, so pushing a v* tag produced no installers for a whole release cycle. A workflow that never runs cannot report its own breakage, so this validates statically what needs no tag, key material, or macOS/Windows runner: action pins, referenced paths, docker residue left by the desktop-only restore, an inventory gate demanding an artifact no matrix entry builds, and that a missing UPDATER_PRIVATE_KEY still hard-fails rather than publishing an unsigned manifest every client rejects. Ships with --self-test (8 mutations) so a regression cannot silently turn it into a no-op.

gates.label: Release readiness
gates._note: Runs scripts/check-updater-compat.mjs, which builds a Rust harness pinned to the minisign-verify version the real Tauri updater client uses and proves that signatures from generate-latest-json.mjs VERIFY, that a tampered installer is REJECTED, and that the pubkey committed in tauri.conf.json parses. Before this it ran ONLY inside release.yml.bak, i.e. nowhere at all -- so the signing chain could have rotted silently alongside the retired workflow and the first symptom would be customers unable to auto-update. Path-gated on the release toolchain and the updater pubkey because the harness needs a cold cargo build. No `runners` key: that field names LOCAL entry points, and this one needs a cargo build, so it is CI-only.
